source_text: I. Imperatore Valeriano quartum et Gallieno tertium consulibus, tertio kalendarum Septembrium, Carthagine in secretario Paternus proconsul Cypriano episcopo dixit: Sacratissimi imperatores Valerianus et Gallienus litteras ad me dare dignati sunt, quibus praeceperunt eos qui Romanam religionem non colunt, debere Romanas caeremonias recognoscere. exquisivi ergo de nomine tuo, quid mihi respondes? Cyprianus episcopus dixit: Christianus sum et episcopus. nullos alios deos novi nisi unum et verum deum, qui fecit caelum et terram, mare et quae sunt in eis omnia. huic deo nos Christiani deservimus, hunc deprecamur diebus ac noctibus pro nobis et pro omnibus hominibus et pro incolumitate ipsorum imperatorum. Paternus proconsul dixit: In hac ergo voluntate perseveras? Cyprianus episcopus respondit: Bona voluntas, quae deum novit, immutari non potest. Paternus proconsul dixit: Poteris ergo secundum praeceptum Valeriani et Gallieni exsul ad urbem Curubitanam proficisci? Cyprianus episcopus dixit: Proficiscor.
pass_a_gloss: With Emperor Valerian consul a fourth time and Gallienus a third time, on the third day before the Kalends of September, at Carthage in the hearing-room, Paternus the proconsul said to Cyprian the bishop: the most sacred emperors Valerian and Gallienus have deigned to give letters to me, in which they ordered that those who do not observe the Roman religion ought to return to the Roman rites. I have therefore made inquiry about your identity; what do you answer to me? Cyprian the bishop said: I am a Christian and a bishop. I know no other gods except the one and true God, who made heaven and earth, the sea and all things which are in them. This God we Christians serve; him we entreat by days and by nights on behalf of ourselves and on behalf of all men and on behalf of the safety of the emperors themselves. Paternus the proconsul said: Do you then persist in this resolve? Cyprian the bishop answered: A good resolve, which knows God, cannot be changed. Paternus the proconsul said: Will you then be able, according to the order of Valerian and Gallienus, to go as an exile to the city of Curubis? Cyprian the bishop said: I will go.
pass_b_english: In the fourth consulship of the Emperor Valerian and the third of Gallienus, on the third day before the Kalends of September, at Carthage in the council-chamber, the proconsul Paternus said to Bishop Cyprian: The most sacred emperors Valerian and Gallienus have deigned to send letters to me, in which they have commanded that those who do not worship the Roman religion must return to the Roman rites.
I have therefore inquired into your identity; what do you answer to me?
Bishop Cyprian said: I am a Christian and a bishop.

The proconsul Paternus said: Do you then stand firm in this purpose?
Bishop Cyprian answered: A good purpose, which knows God, cannot be altered.
The proconsul Paternus said: Can you then, according to the command of Valerian and Gallienus, depart as an exile to the city of Curubis?
Bishop Cyprian said: I will go.

lemmas.gloss: consul, used here in dating formula
to return to or resume here

choices.english: to return to the Roman rites
choices.why: infinitive depends on debere under an imperial order to abandon Christianity, so recognoscere has its resume-an-earlier-practice sense rather than merely notice
ablative of place with administrative noun for the official hearing-room in Carthage, not secrecy in general

choices.term: Bona voluntas, quae deum novit, immutari non potest
choices.english: A good resolve, which knows God, cannot be changed
choices.why: voluntas here is the declared resolve under interrogation, and immutari is passive with moral necessity expressed by non potest
rejected: Good will, which has known God, is unable to be altered
